meta.subtitle: A price-led rebound on a stretched balance sheet: Q2'26 turned profitable, but net debt/EBITDA of 9.0x and a fully priced FY27 keep us at HOLD

analystCommentary:
Dow's second quarter of 2026 turned the income statement around: net sales rose 20% to $12.1 billion and GAAP net income was $802 million, a swing from a loss a year earlier. Price did the work: local price rose by the same proportion while volume fell 1%. We rate the shares HOLD with a target range of $26 to $31 around a Base case of $28.66.

This republish rests on a corrected balance sheet. FY25 total debt was $18.2 billion and net debt $14.3 billion. On trailing figures, net debt/EBITDA is 9.0x and interest coverage is -1.4x, which puts the desk's balance-sheet gate in its WEAK zone and keeps Dow out of the portfolio. The published label comes from the scenarios, which derive HOLD on their own.

The valuation turns on one input: the multiple the market will pay a year from now, when FY27 is the current year, for FY27E EPS of $1.78. Our Base holds today's ~16.1x on that figure, above today's 12.0x current-year multiple, and so lands on today's price. Holding the current-year multiple instead would derive SELL, so the call is close to SELL; the scenario commentary argues both sides. The Bull ($38.48, 25%) keeps EPS at the FY26E level of $2.39 through FY27. The Bear ($20.65, at the same weight) has pricing fall back and the shares return to their 52-week low.

On those weights the expected upside is +1.6% against a bear-case downside of -27.9%. The 4.96% dividend yield sits outside these price-only scenarios and is the main reason to keep holding the shares rather than sell them.

executiveSummary.companyOverview: Dow Inc. is a materials science company founded in 1897 and headquartered in Midland, Michigan. It makes ethylene, propylene, polyethylene and other plastics and chemical intermediates for packaging, infrastructure, mobility and consumer applications. It sells across the United States, Canada, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, India, the Asia Pacific and Latin America. The filing reports three operating segments. Packaging & Specialty Plastics supplies ethylene, propylene, polyethylene, aromatics and ethylene derivatives such as polyolefin elastomers. Industrial Intermediates & Infrastructure covers polyurethanes, chlor-alkali and vinyl, and construction chemicals. Performance Materials & Coatings provides architectural and industrial coatings, silicon metals and siloxanes. Dow reported sales of approximately $40 billion in 2025 and operates manufacturing sites in 29 countries. Headcount was approximately 34,600 at year-end 2025 and approximately 32,800 at June 30, 2026. The business is cyclical and commodity-heavy: FY25 revenue of $40.0 billion was down 7.0% and the year closed with an operating loss.

thesis.body: Dow is a commodity-heavy chemicals producer coming off a loss year. FY25 revenue fell {- 7.0% -} to $40.0 billion, and the company lost $2.6 billion (-$3.70 diluted EPS). Q2'26 returned the company to profit on higher prices, and Transform to Outperform adds a cost and growth lever that does not depend on the cycle. Three facts keep the case balanced rather than bullish. Consensus already expects earnings to step down from FY26 to FY27 as pricing normalizes. The corrected balance sheet carries $14.3 billion of FY25 net debt, enough to put the desk's balance-sheet gate in its WEAK zone. And at ~16.1x FY27E EPS, today's price already discounts the consensus path. We rate the shares HOLD.

catalysts: Transform to Outperform: management now expects more than $1.3 billion of total self-help benefits in 2026 and says the program's impact will ramp into 2027.
Polyethylene pricing: Packaging & Specialty Plastics local price rose 30% year over year in Q2'26, and how long that holds sets the FY26 and FY27 earnings path.
Interest cover: as the 2025 loss quarters roll out of the trailing window, earnings could recover enough to cover interest, a first step out of the WEAK zone.
risks: The recovery is price-led: Q2'26 volume fell 1% while local price rose 20%, so a reversal in prices would hit earnings directly.
Leverage: trailing net debt/EBITDA is 9.0x and trailing interest coverage is negative, which leaves little room if earnings slip again.
Credit standing: the 10-K warns that a ratings change, including failure to maintain an investment grade rating, could raise borrowing costs.
Middle East exposure: Dow's joint ventures in the region have been directly impacted by the conflict, and feedstock and logistics markets remain volatile.

financials.incomeCommentary:
The five-year income statement shows a long slide into FY25. Revenue fell from $56.9 billion in FY22 to $40.0 billion in FY25, {- 7.0% -} lower in FY25 alone. Gross margin compressed from 19.6% in FY21 to 6.3% in FY25. Operating income turned to {- -$2.7 billion -} (operating margin -6.6%), net income to {- -$2.6 billion -} (-$3.70 diluted EPS), and EBITDA fell to $0.2 billion from $11.0 billion in FY21.

Q2'26 broke the trend. Net sales rose {+ 20% +} to $12.1 billion and the quarter's operating margin was 6.2%. Cost of sales fell to 82.1% of net sales from 94.2% a year earlier. GAAP net income was $802 million and GAAP EPS $0.99; operating EPS was $1.44 against a loss of $0.42 a year earlier. The company attributes the {+ $1.7 billion +} year-over-year improvement in Operating EBIT, to $1.6 billion, primarily to higher prices as well as its self-help initiatives. Operating EBITDA, a non-GAAP measure, was $2,312 million against $703 million. Restructuring and asset-related charges were still $503 million in the quarter, and equity earnings were helped by the suspension of Sadara loss recognition.

The trailing view is weaker than the quarter. Trailing gross margin is 9.9%, better than the FY25 level, but trailing operating margin is still -3.0% and trailing net margin -3.1%, because the window still holds the second half of 2025. One strong quarter has improved the run-rate; it has not yet repaired the full-year picture.
financials.balanceCommentary:
Leverage is the binding constraint in this report. Total debt rose from $14.7 billion in FY21 to $18.2 billion in FY25, and net debt from $11.7 billion to $14.3 billion. Most of the increase in net debt had already happened by FY24, when it stood at $14.2 billion. In FY25 cash and short-term investments rose to $3.8 billion from $2.2 billion, which held net debt nearly flat even as gross debt grew. Total equity slipped to $17.5 billion from $21.2 billion at FY22.

Against earnings, the debt is heavy. Trailing net debt/EBITDA is 9.0x and trailing interest coverage is -1.4x. Coverage is negative because trailing operating income is still a loss: the window includes the second half of 2025, part of a year in which EBITDA was barely positive. Q2'26 on its own was far stronger, but the company's Operating EBITDA, noted above, is a non-GAAP figure that excludes significant items, so it is not on the same basis as the trailing ratio and cannot simply replace it.

The desk's balance-sheet gate reads WEAK for these reasons. Dow is a net debtor, since total debt exceeds cash and investments, and both its negative trailing interest coverage and its trailing leverage ratio fall in the gate's WEAK zone. WEAK marks the balance sheet as too stretched to support a buy-side call. It sets an advisory HOLD ceiling, which the portfolio acts on and which keeps Dow out of it, but it does not change the published label, which follows the scenarios. The zone clears only once trailing operating earnings at least cover interest and leverage falls back toward the gate's limit, which needs the 2025 loss quarters to roll out of the window and current earnings to hold.

The gate does not read DISTRESS, and the reason is cash. FY25 cash and short-term investments covered FY25's free-cash-flow shortfall more than twice over; if that cushion thinned while interest is still uncovered, the zone would turn to DISTRESS. Near-term liquidity is otherwise adequate, with a current ratio of 1.97 at FY25 and 1.75 on trailing figures. The pressure is on the cost of debt and on how much room the company has, not on paying near-term bills.
financials.cashflowCommentary:
Cash generation fell through the downturn. Operating cash flow dropped from $7.5 billion in FY22 to $1.0 billion in FY25, while capital expenditure stayed between -$2.4 billion and -$2.9 billion from FY23 to FY25. Free cash flow was {- -$1.4 billion -} in FY25 (FCF margin -3.6%), after roughly breakeven in FY24. Dividends paid fell to $1.5 billion in FY25 from $2.0 billion in FY24, and repurchases stopped (FY25 repurchases $0.00). Even so, the FY25 dividend exceeded free cash flow.

The trailing picture has turned. The trailing FCF yield is 7.7%, above the 4.96% dividend yield, so on trailing figures free cash flow now covers the dividend. Q2'26 operating cash flow was $1,324 million, up $1,794 million from -$470 million a year earlier, which the company attributes primarily to improved earnings.

Two cautions apply to the trailing figure. The window includes Q1'26, and the 10-Q refers to a judgment paid by Nova Chemicals in connection with a legal matter in that quarter. The sources do not show how that payment flowed through cash flow, so part of the trailing free cash flow may not recur. The July 2026 Canada Revenue Agency refund of approximately $318 million (US) is likewise a one-time receipt and falls after the trailing window. Dividend cover in FY27 therefore depends on earnings, not on 2026's receipts, and consensus expects those earnings to be lower than in FY26.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
Trailing multiples do not anchor anything here. The trailing P/E of -15.7x reflects a loss. The trailing EV/EBITDA of 22.3x divides an enterprise value that includes substantial net debt ($14.3 billion at FY25) by EBITDA still depressed by 2025, so it measures the trough and the debt rather than value. P/S is 0.5x, low but typical of a thin-margin year.

The forward multiples are the useful pair, and they sit on different years. The vendor's 12.0x 'NTM' P/E matches the price over FY26E EPS of $2.39, so it is in effect today's current-year multiple. On FY27E EPS of $1.78 the shares trade at ~16.1x. The gap between the two is the consensus step-down in EPS from FY26 to FY27. The scenarios value the shares a year out, when FY27 will be the current year, so the choice between these two multiples is the deciding input, and the scenario commentary argues it.

The price has moved sharply. At $28.65 (September 23, 2026) the shares sit about a third below the 52-week high of $42.74 and well above the low of $20.65. No source in this pack explains either move.

The Street is more constructive than we are. The consensus target is $34.44 (+20.2%), with a median of $34.00 and a range of $29.00 to $41.00, from 19 analysts split six Buy, twelve Hold and one Sell. Our Base sits below the Street's lowest target; the scenario commentary explains why.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Polyethylene pricing holds and Transform to Outperform lands its targeted improvement of at least $2 billion in Operating EBITDA, so EPS stays near the FY26E level of $2.39 through FY27 instead of stepping down. At today's ~16.1x FY27E multiple applied to that EPS, the shares reach $38.48, still below the Street's $41.00 high target and the $42.74 52-week high.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Consensus is delivered: EPS steps down from the FY26E level to $1.78 in FY27E as pricing normalizes, with self-help offsetting part of the decline. A year out the market pays today's FY27E multiple on that EPS, above today's current-year multiple, which gives $28.66, in line with today's price. That multiple is the assumption that decides the label.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: The higher prices behind Q2'26 fall back while competition keeps pressure on price and volume, a risk the 10-K says may worsen in the near term. FY27 EPS falls well short of consensus, toward the FY23-FY24 range of $0.82 to $1.57, and the shares return to their 52-week low of $20.65, a price the market paid within the past year. The dividend would come under pressure in this case.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
We weight Bull 25%, Base 50% and Bear 25%. The weighted value sits close to the current price, for expected upside of +1.6% against a bear-case downside of -27.9% and reward/risk of 0.06×. The derived label is HOLD, and it sits much nearer the SELL line than the BUY line.

The Base decides the label. It assumes that a year out, when FY27 is the current year, the market pays the multiple it pays for FY27E today. That is above today's current-year multiple, so the Base assumes the current-year multiple rises. The case for it: consensus expects EPS to step down from FY26 to FY27, so the market may be treating FY26 as an above-trend year and paying less for it; FY27E EPS is far below the $6.28 and $8.38 Dow earned in FY22 and FY21; and the company expects Transform to Outperform to ramp into 2027, so investors may look through FY27 to a recovery. The Street's median target is consistent with that view. The case against: earnings are falling into FY27, trailing leverage sits in the gate's WEAK zone, and the 10-K expects competitive pressure to continue, none of which argues for a higher multiple.

We hold the FY27E multiple, but the call is close to SELL. Holding today's current-year 'NTM' multiple on FY27E EPS instead would put the Base near the Bear and derive SELL, and a basis about halfway between the two multiples sits at the SELL line. Anchoring the Base to the Street median would lift expected upside above the 10% BUY line but leave reward/risk below 0.50×, so it would still derive HOLD.

The symmetric Bull and Bear weights are a judgment, not a finding. Self-help, the $1 billion of structural cost reductions announced in 2025 and the cost-advantaged U.S. & Canada base make a full return to FY25-style losses less likely. The leverage and the price-led nature of the gain make the downside sharper if it comes. We judge these to offset. Moving ten points of weight from Bear to Bull would not reach the BUY line, and moving ten points the other way would come close to SELL without crossing it.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: The data pack carries Dow as a single consolidated segment, but the 10-Q and the earnings release report three operating segments, and we follow the filing. In Q2'26 Packaging & Specialty Plastics led: net sales were $6,385 million and Operating EBIT rose to $1,278 million from $71 million, which the company credits to higher integrated margins from polyethylene prices and to self-help. Industrial Intermediates & Infrastructure returned to Operating EBIT of $246 million from -$185 million on higher margins, self-help, lower maintenance and the suspended Sadara losses. Performance Materials & Coatings slipped to $133 million from $152 million as higher fixed costs, including turnaround activity and the Barry, U.K. siloxanes shutdown, outweighed self-help. The common thread is that earnings swing mainly with commodity margins rather than with company-specific pricing power.

moatFactors.name: Scale and asset integration
moatFactors.body: Dow operates manufacturing sites in 29 countries, with roughly $40 billion of annual sales and an integrated value chain from ethylene to derivatives. Scale and integration lower unit costs and let the company flex feedstocks, a genuine structural advantage. They do not confer pricing power: the products are largely commodities and margins follow the cycle, as the 6.3% FY25 gross margin shows.

moatFactors.name: Feedstock cost position
moatFactors.body: The company operates in cost-advantaged regions, including the U.S. & Canada and Latin America, which it says have not been directly impacted by the Middle East conflict. It says feedstock flexibility let it run its European assets competitively through a volatile energy environment. This is a durable edge on cost, not on demand or price.

moatFactors.name: Pricing power
moatFactors.body: Prices are set by global supply and demand for commodity chemicals. Q2'26 local price rose 20%, but the same market mechanism drove the FY25 slide to an operating loss. The 10-K says increased competition has already lowered prices and sales volume, and that these pressures may worsen in the near term.

moatFactors.name: Switching costs
moatFactors.body: For commodity grades of polyethylene, polyurethanes and chlor-alkali, customers can buy from multiple global suppliers. Downstream silicones and coatings carry more differentiation, but Performance Materials & Coatings is the smallest of the three segments by Q2'26 net sales.

businessMoat.durability: Dow's advantages are real but narrow. Scale, integration and low-cost feedstock positions give it a cost edge that persists across the cycle, which is why we assign a narrow rather than no moat. The edge cannot stabilize returns. Gross margin fell from 19.6% in FY21 to the FY25 level noted above, operating income turned negative, and FY25 was a net loss. In a commodity business a cost advantage narrows losses at the trough and widens gains at the peak, but it does not remove the cycle. Transform to Outperform targets a leaner cost base. The 10-K calls the Alberta net-zero cracker project a key element in achieving the company's 2030 greenhouse gas emissions reduction commitment, and lists its cost and timing among the risks. The durability question is whether pricing recovers enough for that cost edge to earn an adequate return on capital. The recovery has begun, but one quarter does not prove it.

points: Cyclical rebound: Q2'26 net sales rose 20% year over year to $12.1 billion, with increases in all three segments and all geographic regions; consensus FY26E revenue is about $43.6 billion, up 9%.
The rebound is price-led, not volume-led: local price rose in step with sales while volume fell 1%, with Asia Pacific and EMEAI volumes lower, so growth lasts only as long as pricing holds.

Self-help is the main lever the company controls: Transform to Outperform targets at least $2 billion of near-term Operating EBITDA improvement, but delivered $190 million in the six months to June 2026, and the release does not split the $1.3 billion-plus 2026 self-help total by program.

Structural demand pockets: Industrial Solutions cited alkoxylation investments and data center applications, and Consumer Solutions grew downstream silicones in consumer, electronics and home care applications.
Consensus expects the rebound to fade: FY27E revenue of $42.9 billion is below FY26E, and the valuation section treats the matching EPS step-down as the deciding input.

management.leadership: Leadership changed at the top in mid-2026. On April 14, 2026, the Board appointed Karen S. Carter as Chief Executive Officer effective July 1, 2026. She succeeded Jim Fitterling, who moved from Chief Executive Officer to Executive Chair, and she joined the Board on the same date. In the July 23, 2026 results release, Carter said Dow now expects approximately $200 million more in Transform to Outperform benefits this year. The transition is recent, so delivery of Transform to Outperform in the second half of 2026 is the main test of the new CEO.
management.capitalAllocation: Capital allocation is under strain. In FY25 Dow paid a reduced dividend, repurchased no stock, and still paid out more than it generated in free cash flow; the cash flow section covers how the trailing picture has since turned. The Board declared a $0.35 per share dividend in April 2026, the 459th consecutive dividend paid by the company or its affiliates since 1912, and Q2'26 dividends totaled $253 million. Management names balanced capital allocation as one of its three priorities. It has also raised outside capital at the asset level: InfraPark, a subsidiary of a fund managed by Macquarie Asset Management, bought 40% of Diamond Infrastructure Solutions in Q2'25 and a further 9% in Q3'25. That entity's earnings now flow partly to noncontrolling interests, which took $81 million in Q2'26 against $34 million a year earlier. With leverage where it is, the dividend competes directly with debt reduction for the cash the recovery produces.
management.governance: Governance rests on the DEF 14A proxy statement filed February 27, 2026. The Board determined that eleven director nominees are independent: Samuel R. Allen, Gaurdie E. Banister Jr., Wesley G. Bush, Richard K. Davis, Jerri DeVard, Debra L. Dial, Jeff M. Fettig, Jacqueline C. Hinman, Luis Alberto Moreno, Jill S. Wyant and Daniel W. Yohannes. The proxy says these independent nominees constitute a "substantial majority" of the Board. At the proxy date Mr. Fitterling, then Chair and CEO, was not independent. All members of the Audit, Compensation and Leadership Development, Corporate Governance, and Environment, Health, Safety & Technology committees are independent. The Board has no policy requiring the Chair and CEO roles to be combined or separated and decides annually; the July 2026 split between CEO (Carter) and Executive Chair (Fitterling) fits that flexibility. All incumbent directors were re-elected at the 2026 annual meeting, whose results were announced on April 9, 2026.
management.insiderOwnership: The proxy excerpt in this pack covers board independence, leadership structure and the related-person transaction policy, but not the beneficial-ownership tables, so we quote no insider or 5% holder figure. Related-person transactions are reviewed by the Corporate Governance Committee under written policies that weigh commercial reasonableness, the materiality of the related person's interest and any conflict of interest.

idiosyncratic: Dividend cover in a downturn. Trailing free cash flow now covers the dividend, but part of the trailing cash may not recur and FY25's free cash flow did not cover it. If earnings slip back as in the Bear case while net debt stays near $14.3 billion, the board would have to choose between the payout and the balance sheet.

Price-led recovery. Q2'26 growth came from price while volume fell. Commodity prices can reverse quickly, and the 10-K says competitive pressure on price and volume is expected to continue and may worsen in the near term.

Execution on Transform to Outperform. Most of the program's targeted improvement is still ahead (see Growth), and delivery now rests with a CEO who took over on July 1, 2026. The program's costs are already in the results: Q2'26 restructuring charges included severance tied to it.

Credit standing. Total debt reached $18.2 billion at FY25 and trailing interest coverage is negative. The 10-K, filed February 3, 2026, warns that changes in the company's credit ratings, including failure to maintain an investment grade rating, could increase borrowing costs and reduce sources of liquidity. A second leg down in earnings before they recover enough to cover interest would test that.

Joint-venture stress. Q2'26 equity earnings improved partly because Dow suspended recognizing its share of Sadara joint-venture losses, and the company says its Middle East joint ventures have been directly impacted by the regional conflict.
risks.systemic: Dow is exposed to the global chemicals cycle and to macro conditions it does not control. Energy and feedstock price volatility is a persistent input risk. The 10-Q says the Middle East conflict and tensions affecting the Strait of Hormuz have disrupted energy and petrochemical supply chains, raised transportation and operating costs, and reduced supply chain reliability, particularly in Asia Pacific and Europe. Trade policy is a further overhang: the 10-K says the United States announced significant new tariffs in 2025 on virtually all imported goods, with certain exceptions, and that tariffs and trade-agreement changes could lower sales volume. Climate-related transition costs, and the execution risk of large decarbonization projects such as the Alberta net-zero cracker, sit on the longer horizon.

body: We rate Dow HOLD with a target range of $26 to $31 around a $28.66 Base case. The label follows the scenarios, which derive HOLD, and the call is closer to SELL than to BUY. The Q2'26 rebound is real, but it is price-led, consensus expects part of it to reverse in FY27, and the corrected balance sheet leaves little room if it reverses further. This republish keeps the HOLD label but lowers the target range, because the Base no longer borrows the Street's median target.

On these scenarios, a price at or below the target low would derive BUY, and a price at or above the target high would derive SELL. The WEAK gate does not change the published label, but its advisory HOLD is what the portfolio acts on, so it keeps Dow out of the portfolio and remains a reason for caution until trailing operating earnings at least cover interest and leverage falls back. The input to re-check at the next filing is the Base multiple: evidence that FY27 earnings will hold above consensus, through pricing or self-help, would support today's FY27E multiple, and a further slide in volume would push the Base toward the current-year multiple and a SELL.
